source.title: Beyond Adam: disentangling optimizer effects in the fine-tuning of atomistic foundation models
source.authors: Xiao-Qing Liu; Yang-Shuai Wang; Teng Zhao

record.tranche_reason: Tests optimizer effects on held-out performance in atomistic foundation models, a new model and task setting for V4.
record.gate_note: The study reports held-out energy and force RMSE for optimizer comparisons. It does not test random-label memorization, width, architecture comparisons, batch size, dropout, sharpness measures, or removal of memorized examples. Rows cover all seven optimizers and all four 3BPA conditions in Table 1; the additional Silicon results in Table 2 and the learning-rate ablation in Table C1 are not extracted due to the 60-row limit.
record.test_reason: The study compares held-out errors after fine-tuning neural atomistic models with adaptive optimizers and plain SGD, extending V4's optimizer comparison to a new task. It does not directly retest V4's image or language settings, and the main comparison's tuning protocol is incompletely specified.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors favor AdamW and ScheduleFree for atomistic fine-tuning, describe plain SGD as slow and unstable, and recommend targeted L-BFGS refinement. Their claims of consistent superiority and stable rankings are stronger than the tables: Silicon results are mixed, and Table C1 includes cases where Adam or RAdam has worse force RMSE than SGD.
record.recipe_differences: Fine-tunes pretrained atomistic foundation models on energy and force regression rather than ordinary supervised classification or language benchmarks; compares first-order optimizers and optional L-BFGS refinement.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer choice and test condition (300K, 600K, 1200K, dihedral scan) affect held-out RMSE.

fits_no_version.finding: The preconditioning analysis concerns Hessian conditioning and convergence; physical evaluations concern phonons, elasticity, and molecular dynamics.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer choice and optional L-BFGS refinement affect the conditioning and physical fidelity of fine-tuned atomistic potentials. These are not measurements of V7's magnitude-aware sharpness–generalization-gap correlation.

record.problems: This setting is atomistic foundation-model fine-tuning, so it does not establish optimizer rankings for the image-classification or language tasks specified in V4. The paper reports three-seed standard deviations, but no training RMSE in Table 1 for comparison with held-out error.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 Silicon dataset results for all seven optimizers and Table C1 learning-rate ablation are not extracted; the 60-row cap was used for the seven optimizer outcomes across four 3BPA test conditions and two metrics in Table 1.

untested.parts: Fixed random-label fitting and comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width dependence beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.

Image and language benchmarks; comparable training performance; momentum SGD; controlled broader hyperparameter tuning; switching Adam to SGD; word-level language modeling. AdamW is compared with Adam, but decoupled weight decay is not isolated by a documented matched ablation.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects, small-data regimes, and joint dropout/weight-decay removal with augmentation.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, measured training–test gaps, and rankings against norm or margin measures.
Influence-based selection and removal of memorized training examples.

missing.what: Table 3 base optimizer comparisons for Adam, AdamW, and ScheduleFree across five systems; these extend the AdamW-versus-Adam evidence beyond 3BPA and were not declared in rows_left_out.

record.verdict_notes: All 56 extracted means and standard deviations match Table 1. Reversed states refer to adaptive-versus-SGD held-out error, not to every clause of V4. Training RMSE is unnecessary for that comparison but is needed to establish a difference despite equal or better training performance. The paper does not adequately document the main learning rates, schedules, training budgets, or matched weight-decay settings. Tables 2 and C1 are explicitly declared omitted, so they are not missing entries. Table 2 contradicts the prose that SGD is worst everywhere: stacking-fault force RMSE is 31.7 for SGD, 31.8 for Adam, 39.0 for Ranger, and 34.7 for ScheduleFree. Table C1 also contradicts invariant optimizer rankings: at learning rate 0.005 and 1200 K, force RMSE is 47.7 for SGD, 55.9 for Adam, and 49.5 for RAdam. These declared omissions should be retained when interpreting the study, rather than replacing them with its blanket narrative.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.

Image-classification and language benchmarks; broader hyperparameter tuning; comparison with momentum SGD; effects of decoupled weight decay or switching optimizers beyond the reported AdamW comparison; word-level language models.
Batch-size effects and adaptations to large-batch training.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with the generalization gap.

relationships.condition: 3BPA atomistic-model fine-tuning: 300 K in-distribution and 600 K, 1200 K, and dihedral-scan out-of-distribution tests
relationships.reason: All six adaptive methods have lower mean energy and force RMSE than plain SGD in r01–r56; for example Adam force RMSE is 13.4 versus 27.9 at 300 K. This bounds extension to atomistic fine-tuning, without contradicting the specified image/language results.
relationships.display_finding: For MACE-OFF-23 at 300 K, Adam reduced the root mean squared error (RMSE) in force predictions from SGD's 27.9 to 13.4. The comparison across temperatures has only been partly verified.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: 3BPA atomistic-model fine-tuning: 300 K in-distribution and 600 K, 1200 K, and dihedral-scan out-of-distribution tests
source_check.reason: Table 1 confirms lower mean energy and force RMSE for every adaptive optimizer than for plain SGD across all four conditions. This limits extension of the adaptive disadvantage to atomistic fine-tuning; it does not contradict the named image/language results.

relationships.condition: AdamW versus Adam in 3BPA fine-tuning across all four test conditions
relationships.reason: AdamW has lower mean RMSE on all eight comparisons in r02/r03, r09/r10, r16/r17, r23/r24, r30/r31, r37/r38, r44/r45, and r51/r52, consistent with V4's AdamW recovery clause; the comparison does not isolate weight-decay implementation causally.
relationships.display_finding: AdamW lowers MACE-OFF-23 energy and force RMSE at 300 K and 600 K; the remaining reported comparisons remain unverified.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: AdamW versus Adam in 3BPA fine-tuning across all four test conditions
source_check.reason: Table 1 confirms AdamW has lower mean energy and force RMSE than Adam in all four conditions, consistent with V4's AdamW recovery clause. The comparison does not isolate decoupled weight decay causally.

relationships.condition: AdamW versus Adam before L-BFGS in five additional atomistic systems
relationships.reason: Text-only verdict from Table 3, missing rows: AdamW base force RMSE is lower than Adam for Mo (28.6 versus 32.1), MoS2 (2.2 versus 3.1), LFP (65.4 versus 66.8), ZnO/GaN (7.5 versus 9.2), and graphene–water (10.4 versus 12.2).
relationships.display_finding: Reported AdamW base force RMSE is lower across all five systems, but these comparisons remain unverified and do not isolate weight-decay implementation.

source_check.label: supports

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.condition: 3BPA atomistic-model fine-tuning: 300 K in-distribution and 600 K, 1200 K, and dihedral-scan out-of-distribution tests
labels.reason: Table 1 confirms lower mean energy and force RMSE for every adaptive optimizer than for plain SGD across all four conditions. This limits extension of the adaptive disadvantage to atomistic fine-tuning; it does not contradict the named image/language results.

labels.label: supports
labels.condition: AdamW versus Adam in 3BPA fine-tuning across all four test conditions
labels.reason: Table 1 confirms AdamW has lower mean energy and force RMSE than Adam in all four conditions, consistent with V4's AdamW recovery clause. The comparison does not isolate decoupled weight decay causally.

labels.label: supports
labels.condition: AdamW versus Adam before L-BFGS in five additional atomistic systems
labels.reason: Table 3 confirms lower base force RMSE for AdamW than Adam: Mo 28.6 versus 32.1; MoS2 2.2 versus 3.1; LFP 65.4 versus 66.8; ZnO/GaN 7.5 versus 9.2; graphene–water 10.4 versus 12.2 meV/Å. This is consistent with the recovery clause without establishing its mechanism.

relation.reason: The study directly compares held-out performance under different optimizers, including adaptive methods and plain SGD.

tranche.reason: Held-out energy and force comparisons extend the optimizer-generalization question to pretrained atomistic-model fine-tuning.

source_check.notes: All 25 listed values and uncertainties match Table 1; subjects need the model identity. Silicon and learning-rate results do not sustain the authors' universal ranking claims; Table C1 also differs from Table 1 on some corresponding Adam values.

statements.correction: Table 1: MACE-OFF-23, 3BPA, 300 K test; Adam force RMSE 13.4 (1.70) meV/Å; plain SGD 27.9 (0.06) meV/Å; three seeds. Atomistic fine-tuning: scope-extension evidence; momentum-SGD comparison absent; limited-tuning eligibility unestablished.
statements.problem: The atomistic numbers and stated limitations are accurate, but classifying this result as challenges overstates its bearing on V4's specified image/language regime.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: 3BPA fine-tuning; tested 300K, 600K, 1200K, and dihedral scan conditions
reader_labels.reason: AdamW and ScheduleFree generally have lower held-out energy/force RMSE than Adam, while SGD is reported worst; this atomistic fine-tuning setting does not support a blanket claim that adaptive optimizers generalize worse. Rows r01-r56 provide the optimizer-specific outcomes.
